answer: Disputing a comet sighting reserves a queue slot against $200 until dawn. The ledger admits one appeal per key and assigns each slot a separate escrow. Jurors slide onyx over the lens to test whether a disputed pattern persists in darkness. A signed jury verdict proving fabricated evidence forfeits the bond. One honest user locks $200 and 1,000 concurrent aliases lock $200,000. Valid appeals get their bonds back. At a 1% funding cost per window, carrying those locks costs $2 and $2,000 respectively. Wealthy bots can still crowd the queue, and bad jurors can slash valid claims.
